correctness.rationale: The two-round Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game reduces to the set of pointed one-round atomic diagrams on (e,x,y). The proof checks x=e, the unique involution z=a^n, and order-three/four/large elements with their square-root types. The order-three existence 3|n, rootable order-four existence 4|n, and large square-order existence n>=5 yield seven spectra and representatives 2,3,4,5,6,8,12. Independently enumerated all atomic diagrams n=2..18, recovered exactly the predicted seven signatures. Finite enumeration corroborates, but the uniform congruence analysis proves infinitely many n.
